headline: Highest risk is medium: Goose can write/egress while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only, creating default prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways through shared filesystem use.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem, use MCP, and has no default self-isolation; python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and cannot actively defend itself. The pair shares a filesystem pathway via Goose’s concurrency model, so attacker-controlled file content could be treated as instructions if copied into Goose workflows. This is plausible in default coding setups, though not guaranteed.
conditions: IF Goose ingests files from the shared cwd as instructions or prompts, injection is possible.
IF python-cheatsheet content is copied into Goose without sanitization, malicious markup can steer tool use.
mitigations: Keep the shared workspace read-only for the documentation agent.
Require manual review before Goose reads any file produced by the other agent.
Strip instructions from copied text before pasting into Goose.
Use separate directories per agent.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd, and its network egress is broad; python-cheatsheet is local-only documentation with no network or file access. If both operate on the same workspace, Goose can expose file contents to external model providers, creating a default leakage path for sensitive code or secrets present in cwd. The other agent does not add protection.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared cwd, Goose can transmit them to configured providers.
IF the documentation agent is used to summarize or copy those files, the same data can be re-exposed in outputs.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the shared workspace.
Run Goose with a redacted working directory.
Disable provider access for tasks that do not need it.
Use separate OS users or containers.
requires-engineering: enforce per-file allowlists before model upload.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose can write the filesystem and modify git state; python-cheatsheet cannot write or modify anything. There is no direct write-write conflict, but Goose’s shared-state-via-filesystem model means concurrent instances can collide on the same workspace if the operator runs multiple copies. Because the pair includes one mutable agent and one inert agent, the conflict risk is real but not high.
conditions: IF multiple Goose instances target the same repo or cwd, file and git collisions can occur.
IF the documentation agent is manually edited into the same workspace, Goose may overwrite its files.
mitigations: Assign each Goose session a separate working tree.
Avoid concurrent git operations on the same branch.
Use file locks for shared artifacts.
Keep the documentation agent outside the writable repo.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can act on files and git state, while python-cheatsheet is a reference artifact that may be treated as authoritative content. If Goose’s output is copied into the documentation workflow or vice versa, errors can propagate from generated text into downstream actions or commits. The pair lacks a built-in verification loop, so the default risk is a mistaken action chain rather than a catastrophic one.
conditions: IF Goose-generated text is used as source material for the documentation agent, errors can be preserved.
IF Goose commits or edits files based on unverified summaries, downstream mistakes can be persisted.
mitigations: Require human verification before commits.
Mark generated text as untrusted in filenames or headers.
Compare outputs against source files before actioning them.
Keep the documentation agent read-only.
requires-engineering: add a verification step before any git write.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no data handling. Goose does handle model-provider keys and extension tokens, so compliance concerns are mostly about operator-managed secrets rather than a pairwise policy breach. The other agent is not a compliance driver here.
conditions: IF Goose is configured to process regulated data under a provider without the required controls, compliance risk increases.
IF the shared workspace contains restricted data and Goose uploads it externally, policy violations can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Goose tasks.
Review provider terms before enabling sensitive workflows.
Store secrets outside the workspace.
Use a local-only model for restricted projects.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention for each provider.
